A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEL framework and experiments. All pages, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including the added Appendix F in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Brownian-motion and double-well simulations, quantitative shape-process comparisons, and conditional Fashion-MNIST samples in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds a conditioned shape-process trajectory illustration in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The BEL losses, weighting variants, training procedure and adjoint computation remain unchanged. The score-matching objective highlighted in v2 already appears in v1 Appendix B; revised explanations do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate one- and ten-dimensional Brownian and double-well bridges, stochastic shape processes, and Fashion-MNIST corner conditioning. The added shape illustration uses the existing circle-target task; new introductory application examples are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Controlled experiments retain the same four BEL variants and Reparametrization Trick. Shape comparisons retain Time reversal, Adjoint paths and Untrained alongside BEL average. The additional methods discussed in Appendix F are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains the discretisation, architectures, training budgets, metrics and evaluation counts, including 15,000 controlled-environment simulations and 512 shape trajectories. The replacement illustration does not establish a change to the stated experimental protocol.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 8 extends v1's unconditioned shape illustration into a qualitative comparison with a BEL-average trajectory conditioned toward the target circle. Existing weighting-variant and dimensional comparisons remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds training-seed information, repeated-training estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Evaluation sample counts and the existing mean-and-variance trajectory metric are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the unconditioned shape example and adds a conditioned trajectory in Figure 8. Numerical tables remain unchanged after matching relocations and renumbering; Table 1 still reports 0.085 for BEL average and 0.090 for Time reversal.

T1.justification: v2 revises the loss/minimiser statement in Lemma 3.3 and corrects conditioning and differentiation indices in Appendix D.1, while consolidating existing martingale lemmas. Appendix F adds a Bayes score identity with an erroneous plus sign before the marginal score. The central theorems and variance analysis remain.

C1.justification: The substantive claims about singular-reward conditioning, generalised Tweedie scores and performance are retained. v2 foregrounds post-hoc diffusion-model control, score matching and possible geometric extensions, but these contributions were already described in v1 Section 4.3, Remarks 2.4–2.5 and Appendix B.

C2.justification: Remark B.2 explains geometric extensions more specifically and adds a qualification about compatibility between Wiener processes and Hilbert-space norms. Appendix F expands the discussion of approximate guidance, posterior fidelity and inaccurate or fine-tuned score networks beyond v1's shorter discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C retain the adjoint implementation, network layers, optimiser, training counts, kernel parameters and evaluation instructions. Baseline-code attribution is unchanged, and no new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: New Appendix F substantially expands research positioning: it covers classical bridge samplers, posterior-guidance methods and concurrent Malliavin studies by Mirafzali et al. and Greco, explaining differences in objectives and derivative requirements. The introduction also adds Bayesian inverse-problem and conditional-control context.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are rewritten, introductory guidance explanations are expanded, and several remarks and appendix lemmas are reorganised. These are targeted narrative revisions; most methodological and experimental exposition retains its structure.

P2.justification: The double-well tables move from the main text to Appendix C, and the Brownian table display is relabelled from Figure 8 to Table 4. The single shape plot becomes a two-panel comparison with revised axes and target markers. Figures 1–7 retain their visual data.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies amortised conditioning, provides fuller context for assessing novelty, and adds an informative conditioned-shape illustration. These provide a limited overall gain while the methods, numerical evidence and reproducibility information remain stable. The new sign error in Appendix F's score identity detracts from mathematical precision, but is confined to the added contextual discussion.
